text:
Maria L: quick 🔎 — running into a weird combo of issues when using the Node TS SDK in a Next.js edge route + Vite dev server. Two things: auth fallback isn't picking up `REDWOOD_API_KEY` in edge runtime, and streaming responses are failing with `TypeError: body.getReader is not a function`. anyone seen this?

Jonathan K: hmm — for the edge route are you running in Next's actual Edge runtime (i.e. `export const runtime = 'edge'`)? env var access is different there (no process.env at runtime).

Maria L: yep runtime set to 'edge'. I have `REDWOOD_API_KEY` in vercel/environment vars. On serverless pages it reads fine, only edge routes fail.

Sasha P: Edge runtimes don't have Node `process.env` at runtime — Next injects envs at build time. You need to reference `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY` during build or use Next's server runtime config: `next.config.js` with `env` or `publicRuntimeConfig`? For Edge specifically, we recommend using the SDK with a fetch-based auth header: set `authorization` via middleware at the edge.

Maria L: ah ok. So best practice: pass key to client on build and attach header in the route? worried about leaking key to client.

Sasha P: don't put secret in client bundle. Instead on Edge route assemble server-side fetch with header. Example: `const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY } })` — call SDK low-level fetch if you must. Alternatively, run a tiny serverless function (server runtime) that proxies to the hosted API.

Oliver: on the streaming issue — `body.getReader` is a browser stream thing. The SDK's streaming helper expects a WHATWG ReadableStream in edge/Browser but Node has a different stream. In Node 18+ there is global `ReadableStream` but some bundlers polyfill/replace it. Vite dev mode will sometimes wrap modules so the SDK ends up calling the wrong stream API.

Maria L: stack trace shows `TypeError: body.getReader is not a function` from `streaming.ts:42` inside the SDK. I'm using `type: "module"` in package.json and vite 4.2.

Jonathan K: two angles: 1) make sure you're not bundling the SDK for edge — for Next edge routes you want the SDK as an external import so the runtime's native streams are preserved; 2) ensure Node/Vercel Edge runtime has WHATWG streams. For Vite, try `ssr: { noExternal: ['@redwood/inference'] }` if you *want* bundling, or the opposite `optimizeDeps.exclude`/`ssr.external` to keep it external. For Next, use `webpack: config.externals = ['@redwood/inference']` in `next.config.js` for edge serverless? (works differently per platform).

Sasha P: concrete snippets: Vite (vite.config.ts):
```
export default defineConfig({
  ssr: {
    noExternal: ['@redwood/inference'] // prevents Vite from pre-bundling this lib in dev
  }
})
```
Or to *not* bundle the SDK: `ssr.external = ['@redwood/inference']`. Try both if unsure.

Maria L: thanks — I'm bundling currently, maybe that's why. Any CJS/ESM gotchas? package.json has `type: \"module\"` so imports are `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'`. But some lambda layers expect CJS.

Oliver: yep — the SDK ships dual ESM/CJS. If your bundler resolves to the CJS build (or vice versa) you can get `module.exports` vs `export default` mismatches. Quick check: in Node REPL `node -p "require('module').createRequire(import.meta.url)('./node_modules/@redwood/inference/package.json').exports"` will show resolution. Simpler: try both import styles in a repro: `const mod = await import('@redwood/inference'); console.log(Object.keys(mod))` — see if default export present.

Maria L: ok that repro helps. For Next edge we probably want the ESM entrypoint. How do we force that?

Jonathan K: Node's ESM resolution uses `exports`/`module` fields in package.json. If that fails, use dynamic import (`await import('@redwood/inference')`) from an ESM file. Also ensure `next.config.js` isn't transpiling `node_modules` copy of the SDK.

Sasha P: one more tip for streaming in Node dev: if you get `getReader` error, polyfills might have replaced `ReadableStream`. Quick debug: `console.log(globalThis.ReadableStream?.toString?.())` in the route. On Vercel Edge it should be native. If not native, try to avoid bundling or add a tiny compatibility wrapper that converts Node stream to WHATWG stream.

Maria L: great. For auth retry behavior: we're seeing 401 then a retry that fails with the same token. Are retries broken in edge?

Oliver: retries use exponential backoff and don't rotate keys. If 401 is returned, SDK won't retry by default (treats 401 as auth error). If your token is missing due to runtime env issue you'll get 401 every time. There's a config flag `retryOnNetworkError` vs `retryOnServerError`. 401 won't be retried unless you supply a custom `shouldRetry` callback.

Maria L: got it. So first fix env auth in edge, then tackle bundler/streaming. Thanks — I'll try `ssr.external` and dynamic import, and report back.

devex-bot: :thumbsup: If you hit a reproducible minimal repo, ping #devex and we'll schedule a quick pairing session.

Maria L: will do — uploading a tiny repro now. Thanks all!
